mainTopic: Does a נדר compare to an item's original status or its current status? תרומת לחמי תודה and the 'like a בכור' dispute
overview: When someone makes a נדר by comparing food to something holy, does he mean the item's original, forbidden status or its status right now? רבינא tries to prove from the משנה that he means the original status, because תרומת לחמי תודה is only taken after זריקת דמים, when it is already permitted to כהנים. The גמרא rejects this proof in two ways. First, the משנה's hint may point to תרומת הלשכה, which is always forbidden. A short question and answer shows that the משנה's word 'תרומתו' itself means תרומת לחמי תודה. Second, תרומת לחמי תודה can be separated during kneading, before זריקת דמים, while it is still forbidden. שמואל's ruling that four loaves are valid backs this up, since with four loaves the תרומה can only be taken properly from the dough at kneading. The גמרא then suggests that our question matches a מחלוקת between רבי יעקב and רבי יהודה about a נדר 'like a בכור'. It begins to show that neither the 'before' case nor the 'after' case explains both opinions, and its conclusion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבינא's proof: תרומת לחמי תודה comes after זריקת דמים
steps.stepSummary: רבינא points out that תרומת לחמי תודה is only taken after זריקת דמים, when it is already permitted to כהנים. So a נדר comparing food to it must be relying on its original forbidden status.
steps.simpleTranslation: But תרומת לחמי תודה is only separated after זריקת דמים!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא has just drawn an inference from the משנה: comparing food to תרומת לחמי תודה makes the food forbidden. Now he points out a fact about that תרומה, and the fact turns his inference into a proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the time תרומת לחמי תודה is taken, the blood has been sprinkled and the loaves are permitted to כהנים. If a נדר comparing food to it still works, the person must mean its earlier, forbidden status. That would show that a person making a נדר has the original status of the item in mind.

keyTerms.meaning: The loaves set aside for the כהן from the breads brought with a thanks-offering
Sprinkling of the blood on the מזבח, which makes the offering's parts permitted
'But surely…'; introduces a point that builds an argument

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the heart of רבינא's attempt to settle whether a נדר looks at an item's original status or its present status.

phrases.english: But the teruma of the thanks-offering loaves —
is only after the sprinkling of the blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבינא's inference from the משנה (made just before this section) by adding the timing of the teruma.
steps.raayaObject: A person making a נדר refers to the item's original, forbidden status.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's implied ruling that comparing food to תרומת לחמי תודה works, combined with the fact that this teruma is only taken after זריקת דמים.

steps.title: Rejection: the משנה's hint may refer to the Temple chamber collection
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה's hint may point to someone who said 'like תרומת הלשכה', which is always forbidden. It need not point to תרומת לחמי תודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: the inference is that 'like תרומת הלשכה' is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down רבינא's inference by reading the משנה's hint differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא's proof depended on the משנה implying that comparing to תרומת לחמי תודה is forbidden. The גמרא says the implied forbidden case could be תרומת הלשכה instead, and that is forbidden at all times. With that reading, there is no case here of a permitted item, and the proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: The money collected into the בית המקדש chamber, which is always forbidden for personal use

phrases.english: Say: 'like the teruma of the chamber' — is forbidden.
phrases.notes: This is the coins collected for the בית המקדש, which are also called 'teruma'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבינא's proof by changing which case the משנה's hint refers to.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the inference from the משנה, not the timing fact about the teruma.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The forbidden case the משנה implies could be תרומת הלשכה, which is forbidden at all times, rather than תרומת לחמי תודה.

steps.title: Challenge: then the משנה should have taught the thanks-offering loaves
steps.stepSummary: If comparing to תרומת לחמי תודה leaves the food permitted, the משנה should have taught the loaves themselves. Then we would know 'all the more so' about plain תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, תרומת לחמי תודה — is it permitted? If so, the משנה should teach 'לחמי תודה,' and all the more so תרומתו!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rejection from Step 2 by asking what the ruling would be for תרומת לחמי תודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the new reading, a נדר comparing to תרומת לחמי תודה leaves the food permitted. If so, that is the bigger news, so the משנה should have said it outright. The simpler case of 'תרומתו' (תרומת אהרן) would then follow on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Let it teach'; the משנה should have said

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל תְּרוּמַת לַחְמֵי תוֹדָה מַאי — מוּתָּר?
phrases.english: But the teruma of the thanks-offering loaves, what — is it permitted?
Let it teach 'thanks-offering loaves,'
and all the more so his teruma!
phrases.notes: 'His teruma' is a word from the משנה itself: 'like the teruma of אהרן or like his teruma.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל תְּרוּמַת לַחְמֵי תוֹדָה מַאי מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading offered in Step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading in Step 2, which leaves תרומת לחמי תודה permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the stronger case (לחמי תודה) is permitted, the משנה should have taught it, and the weaker case would follow by כל שכן.

steps.title: Answer: 'תרומתו' in the משנה means תרומת לחמי תודה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's word 'תרומתו' itself means תרומת לחמי תודה. The משנה is teaching that this teruma counts as 'his teruma', so it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it teaches us: תרומת לחמי תודה counts as 'תרומתו.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The משנה already mentions this case, in the word 'תרומתו'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does teach that comparing to תרומת לחמי תודה leaves the food permitted. It just uses the word 'תרומתו' to say so. The new point is that this תרומה is what the משנה calls 'תרומתו', so the reading from Step 2 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: 'His teruma'; here it refers to תרומת לחמי תודה

steps.confusionAlert: 'תרומתו' in the משנה does not repeat תרומת אהרן. It refers to a different תרומה, the one taken from לחמי תודה.

phrases.english: This is what it teaches us:
the teruma of the thanks-offering loaves — it is 'his teruma.'

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה never mentions the thanks-offering loaves, so it should have.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's word 'תרומתו' refers to תרומת לחמי תודה and rules it permitted, so it does teach this case.

steps.title: Second rejection: the teruma can be separated before the blood is sprinkled
steps.stepSummary: A second way to reject רבינא's proof: תרומת לחמי תודה can be separated during kneading, before זריקת דמים. A נדר made then compares to something that is still forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you prefer: תרומת לחמי תודה can also be before זריקת דמים, for example, when he separated it during kneading.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to רבינא's proof. This time it attacks the timing fact itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא assumed this תרומה only exists after זריקת דמים. But it can be separated while the dough is kneaded, before the blood is sprinkled. At that point the loaves are forbidden to everyone, so the נדר works without relying on any original status. The proof falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you wish, say'; introduces another answer

steps.whatToRemember: רבינא's proof is rejected twice. First, the משנה's hint may refer to תרומת הלשכה. Second, תרומת לחמי תודה can be separated before זריקת דמים, while it is still forbidden.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
the teruma of the thanks-offering loaves also
can be before the sprinkling of the blood.
For example, where he separated them during kneading.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different rejection of רבינא's proof from Step 1, apart from Steps 2-4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the timing assumption behind רבינא's proof.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The teruma can be separated during kneading, before זריקת דמים, while the loaves are still forbidden.

steps.title: שמואל: a thanks-offering baked as four loaves is valid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings שמואל's ruling that someone who baked the לחמי תודה as only four loaves has still fulfilled his obligation. This will show that תרומה can be taken during kneading.
steps.simpleTranslation: This fits what רב טובי בר קיסנא said in the name of שמואל: if someone baked the thanks-offering loaves as just four loaves, he has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling of שמואל to back up step 5's claim that תרומת לחמי תודה can be separated during kneading. The ruling is the setup; the next steps work out why it proves the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 said the תרומה can be taken from the dough before זריקת דמים. שמואל's case of only four loaves will turn out to work only if the תרומה was taken at kneading, so it proves that this really happens.

keyTerms.meaning: The loaves brought together with a thanks-offering

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי הָא דְּאָמַר רַב טוֹבִי בַּר קִיסְנָא
phrases.english: And this is like what Rav Tovi bar Kisna said
phrases.notes: "This" means the idea from step 5, that the תרומה can be taken while the dough is being kneaded.

phrases.english: that Shmuel said:
Thanks-offering loaves that one baked
as four loaves, he has fulfilled his obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי הָא דְּאָמַר רַב טוֹבִי בַּר קִיסְנָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for step 5's claim that separating at kneading is possible.
steps.raayaObject: That תרומת לחמי תודה can be separated during kneading, before זריקת דמים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's ruling, quoted by רב טובי בר קיסנא, that four loaves are valid.

steps.title: But the Torah requires forty loaves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל: forty loaves are required, so how can four be enough?
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written that there must be forty loaves!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל's ruling, because the requirement is forty loaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תודה needs ten loaves of each of four kinds, forty in total. Four loaves seems to fall far short of that.

phrases.english: But isn't it written that there are forty!

steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that four loaves are enough.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The required number is forty, so four should not be valid.

steps.title: Forty is only the ideal way
steps.stepSummary: Forty loaves are the best way to do the מצוה, but four still fulfill the obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: Forty is for doing the מצוה in the best way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that forty loaves is the ideal, not a requirement for being valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two levels: the best way to do the מצוה (forty), and the minimum that still counts (four, one of each kind). שמואל was talking about the minimum.

keyTerms.meaning: For doing the מצוה in the best way, not required after the fact

phrases.english: It is for the ideal fulfillment of the מצוה.
phrases.notes: After the fact, four loaves still count, one of each kind.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the ideal from what is valid after the fact.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Forty loaves are needed for the offering to be valid.
steps.terutzMaskana: Forty is the ideal; four loaves, one of each kind, are valid after the fact.

steps.title: How can תרומה be taken from only four loaves?
steps.stepSummary: The תרומה must be one whole loaf of each kind. With only four loaves, taking one loaf for all of them is not allowed, and taking slices is not allowed either.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he has to take תרומה! If you say he takes one loaf for all of them, we learned that he may not take from one kind for another. If you say he takes a slice from each, we learned that he may not take a slice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question about שמואל's case: with only four loaves, there seems to be no allowed way to take the תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה, learning from 'אחד מכל קרבן', teaches two rules: each kind needs its own תרומה, and the תרומה must be a whole loaf. With one loaf per kind, giving a whole loaf would leave nothing of that kind, and both other options are ruled out.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, the portion of the תודה loaves given to the כהן

steps.confusionAlert: This is not regular תרומה from produce. It is the part of the תודה loaves that goes to the כהן.

phrases.english: But he needs to take teruma!
And if you say that he takes
one loaf for all of them,
but didn't we learn: 'One out of each offering' —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:14. Each 'offering' here means each of the four kinds of loaves.

phrases.english: that he may not take from one offering for another!
And if you say that he takes
a slice from each and every one,
but didn't we learn: 'One' —
that he may not take a slice!
phrases.notes: The word 'one' teaches that it must be a whole loaf.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 8 accepts the four-loaf case, the גמרא asks how its תרומה works.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both ways of taking תרומה from four finished loaves break the rules learned from 'אחד מכל קרבן'.

steps.title: The תרומה was taken from the dough during kneading
steps.stepSummary: He separated the תרומה from each of the four kinds of dough during kneading, and then baked the rest as four loaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he separated them during kneading: one from the חמץ, one from the חלות, one from the רקיקים, and one from the רבוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the תרומה was taken from the dough of each kind before baking. This also proves step 5's point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Separating at kneading lets each kind give its own whole portion and still leaves one loaf of each kind. Kneading happens before זריקת דמים, so a נדר made then compares to something still forbidden, and רבינא's proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Flour soaked in hot water and mixed with oil

steps.whatToRemember: תרומת לחמי תודה can be taken at kneading, before זריקת דמים. So the משנה's case may be a נדר made then, and it does not prove that a נדר compares to the original status.

phrases.english: Rather, he separated them during kneading.
He took one from the leavened bread,
and one from the loaves,
phrases.notes: These are the unleavened loaves, one of the four kinds.

phrases.english: and one from the wafers,
and one from the scalded dough mixed with oil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9 and so confirms step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moving the separation to an earlier stage.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תרומה is taken from the finished, baked loaves.
steps.terutzMaskana: It was taken from each kind of dough at kneading, before זריקת דמים.

steps.title: Maybe this matches a dispute about vowing 'like a firstborn'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the question of original versus current status is the same as a מחלוקת תנאים about someone who says 'like a בכור'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is like a מחלוקת תנאים? If someone says 'this is upon me like a בכור', רבי יעקב forbids it and רבי יהודה permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new line. It suggests that our question, original status or current status, is already argued by תנאים. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור's meat is eaten by כהנים, so it can be seen as forbidden or as permitted. רבי יעקב forbids the vowed food, maybe because he looks at its original holy status. רבי יהודה permits it, maybe because he looks at its current status.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say this is like a dispute between תנאים?
A firstborn animal, which is holy

phrases.english: Let us say this is like a dispute of tanna'im:
'This is upon me like a firstborn' —
Rabbi Ya'akov forbids,
and Rabbi Yehuda permits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבינא's proof is rejected, the גמרא looks for the question in a מחלוקת תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a נדר 'like a בכור', רבי יעקב forbids and רבי יהודה permits. The גמרא suggests this may be the same question of original versus current status.

steps.title: When exactly is the person comparing his item to a בכור?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the מחלוקת is about. Before זריקת דמים, the permitting opinion makes no sense. After זריקת דמים, the forbidding opinion makes no sense. It then begins to give its own answer with 'אלא לאו.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we talking about? If he compared his item to a בכור before its blood was sprinkled, why would anyone say it is permitted? If he compared it to a בכור after its blood was sprinkled, why would anyone say it is forbidden? So must it not be...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is checking which case the מחלוקת about 'like a בכור' is talking about. It shows that neither simple case works, and this sets up the next move, which begins with 'אלא לאו.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before זריקת דמים, a בכור is clearly holy and forbidden, so the opinion that permits is hard to explain. After זריקת דמים, the כהן may eat it, so the opinion that forbids is hard to explain. Since both simple readings fail, the גמרא is about to say the argument must be about whether we look at the בכור's original status or its current status.

keyTerms.meaning: What are the circumstances? What case is this?
Sprinkling the animal's blood on the מזבח
Rather, is it not...? This opens the גמרא's own suggested answer.

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether a בכור is holy. Everyone agrees about that. The question is which moment in the בכור's life the person had in mind when he made his נדר.

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If we say it is before the sprinkling of the blood,
phrases.notes: Before the blood is sprinkled, the בכור is holy and nobody may eat it.

phrases.english: what is the reason of the one who permits?
And if it is after the sprinkling of the blood,
what is the reason of the one who forbids?
Rather, is it not...

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Checks which case the מחלוקת from step 11 is about, in order to prove the comparison suggested there.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the מחלוקת about a vow made before זריקת דמים or after it?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Neither simple case explains both opinions. This leads to 'אלא לאו,' which introduces the idea that the argument is about original versus current status.
